headline: Council Delay Fails to Hold as Survey Act Clears Override
dek: Four seats slowed the near-system survey; the Arbiter declined to call it a protected matter, and the Assembly found its two-thirds.

illustration.alt: Line drawing of radio telescope dishes beneath a field of stars.
illustration.caption: Instruments of the kind the survey consortium intends to commission.

body: The first test of the Council's suspensive power ended where the treaty says it should: on the Assembly floor, with a two-thirds vote.

The [[DEMO-B-T1-001|Near-System Survey and Preservation Act]] passed in Week 3 by 408 to 144. Within the 48-hour window, the seats of the United States, China, the frontier laboratories and the other middle powers [[DEMO-B-T1-001-CA1|delayed it]], arguing that preservation zones could catch missions already in flight.

The delaying seats had hoped for more than a delay. They asked the [[INST-ARBITER|Arbiter]] to classify the Act as a restriction on established holdings — one of the four matters on which an affected seat holds an entrenched veto. The Arbiter [[DEMO-B-T1-001-R1|declined]], pointing to the Act's fourth provision, which leaves antecedent holdings untouched.
In Week 4 the override carried by 456 to 144 against a requirement of 400 ([[DEMO-D-T1-003]]). The Proprietarian Electra bloc, which had abstained on passage, voted to override.
The Act's 0.8000 units are now committed. No probe has moved. As the Act itself notes, passing a bill does not teleport anything anywhere.
